days.why: the class as it opens, 29 September 1835, with nothing injected: the Guadalupe up in the west, rain over the centre, a fair east
rain falling, the light flat and grey, the ground dark with it, the creeks up
the record's own signature: the wind hard out of the north, the sky clear, the light thin and blue
a norther that brought its rain with it, as the one of 20 November did: wind, cold and rain at once
heavier rain, a dark sky, lightning seen at a distance - 4 November 1835 at San Felipe, "cold and stormy" (HIST-TEX-222)
a low veil on the bottoms and the river, and nothing hidden under it
the wettest day this class ever has: the rivers of the centre at 0.84, full and brown, the bottoms dark
a ford shut: no day of this class quite reaches 0.85, so this one river is raised by hand to show what a student would see if it did
a norther a quarter of an hour old: it comes up rather than flicking on
